newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Five ex-contras dead in Nicaragua combat.
newsitem.headline: Five ex-contras dead in Nicaragua combat.

text.p: Five former contra rebels were killed and two civilians were injured in a clash with the Nicaraguan army, army officials said on Thursday.
The combat took place on a rugged and remote mountainside on Wednesday outside the town of Kuskwaas, about 150 miles (250 km) north of Managua, the army said.

The dead rebels belong to the Northern Front 3-80, descendents of the U.S.-armed contra rebel army that fought the leftist former Sandinista government in the 1980s. The army provided no details about the injured civilians.

"They were outside the peace zone and the army has orders to combat all those who are outside," army spokesman Capt. Milton Sandoval told Reuters, referring to pockets set up for the estimated 700 remaining rebels to disarm.
On May 30, the rebels signed a peace pact with the government, pledging to disarm by last Sunday, but they have since turned defiant.

Heavily armed bands, many armed with leftover weapons from the war, have lingered in Nicaragua seven years after the fighting ended, periodically clashing with the army, whose entire command structure is left over from the Sandinista regime.

Although right-wing President Arnoldo Aleman, who took office on Jan. 10, is sympathetic to the old contra cause, the rebels remain armed in a bid to gain land and credits. However, some political analysts say they simply cannot give up the guerrilla lifestyle.
